mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous sharp week-on-week collapse in RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT and WORKPLACES alongside a spike in RESIDENTIAL indicates a new mobility-restriction regime (e.g., tightened safe-distancing rules). Such coordinated multi-category shocks typically persist for at least two weeks before any easing, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 15 points WoW and PARKS falls more than 10 points WoW in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:all four categories drop sharply in t-0w while RESIDENTIAL rises
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers to within 5 points of its t-1w level within two weeks despite WORKPLACES and PARKS remaining suppressed, indicating the coordinated drop was not a persistent restriction-driven regime.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility directly drives adjacent retail and recreation footfall through commuter-linked shopping (lunch breaks, after-work errands). A sustained depressed WORKPLACES level over the next four weeks will mechanically keep RETAIL_REC lower than its prior four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from 2.0 to -26.6 in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its trailing four-week mean even though WORKPLACES remains below -20 for the full four-week forward window.

mechanism_narrative: A joint spike in RESIDENTIAL combined with a sharp drop in TRANSIT signals a behavioral shift toward staying home rather than commuting for discretionary trips. The interaction of these two signals amplifies suppression of RETAIL_REC beyond what either series would predict alone, because reduced transit use compounds with increased home-dwelling to eliminate casual shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 10 points while TRANSIT falls below -15 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL jumped to 14.7 and TRANSIT fell to -21.4 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 and TRANSIT remains below -15, showing the interaction does not predict further suppression.

mechanism_narrative: The prior three weeks showed only mild RETAIL_REC decline (-2.3 to -3.7) before an abrupt one-week drop to -13.7. Such a single-week outlier against a stable short trend is often a transient shock rather than a new baseline, implying partial mean reversion of RETAIL_REC toward its t-1w to t-3w range within one week.
candidate_trigger: single-week RETAIL_REC decline exceeds twice the average weekly decline of the prior three weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved only -2.3, -1.9, -3.7 over three weeks then dropped to -13.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains at or below -13.7 for the next two consecutive weeks instead of reverting toward the -2 to -4 range.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains persistently elevated (39-43%) and stable even as RETAIL_REC collapses, suggesting restrictions are selectively targeting non-essential recreation and retail rather than essential shopping. This differential policy enforcement should keep the RETAIL_REC-GROCERY_PHARM gap wide over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed between 39 and 43 while RETAIL_REC fell to -13.7
regime_hint: selective policy targeting of non-essential activity
failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC narrows by more than half over the next four weeks, indicating restrictions are not differentially applied.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden week-on-week drop in TRANSIT of more than 20 points indicates reduced commuting and transit-linked retail visits. If TRANSIT stays depressed for a further week, commuting-adjacent retail footfall captured in RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 for a second consecutive week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -2.9 to -21.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds above its t-1w level within two weeks even though TRANSIT remains below -15.

mechanism_narrative: The combined collapse of WORKPLACES and rise of RESIDENTIAL reflects a durable shift toward remote-work lifestyles. This interaction reduces office-district retail and recreation spending structurally, not just transiently, and should keep RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week average for a full four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -20 and RESIDENTIAL above 10 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -26.6 and RESIDENTIAL rose to 14.7 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC returns to or exceeds its trailing four-week mean while WORKPLACES stays below -20 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 10, disproving the interaction's predictive power.

mechanism_narrative: The steep and accelerating decline in PARKS (-11.7 to -37.0 over four weeks) may partly reflect seasonal outdoor-activity suppression (e.g., inter-monsoon rains common in Singapore in October) rather than policy alone. If this seasonal effect dominates while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES partially recover, displaced outdoor activity could shift toward indoor retail, lifting RETAIL_REC modestly within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS continues declining while TRANSIT or WORKPLACES stabilize or rise week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell steadily each week reaching -37.0 while other categories show mixed movement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline in the next week even as PARKS keeps falling and TRANSIT/WORKPLACES show any stabilization or recovery.
